newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower as soybeans falter, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower as soybeans falter, weather.

text.p: CBOT corn closed lower on a break in soybeans and new crop December touched a session low of $2.92-1/2 per bushel, the lowest level for that contract since January 26 when $2.88-1/2 was reached, traders said.
"Basically we've dodged the bullet. Weather is perfect. Enough said, we're going down," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Monday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook was for above to much above normal temperatures in the U.S. Midwest and for normal to no precipitation from October 6 through October 10.
That weather pattern should boost harvest progress and enhance development of the U.S. corn crop.

Corn also was pressured by an improvement in the condition rating for the crop during the latest week. USDA Monday said the U.S. corn crop as of Sunday was 65 percent good to excellent, up from 62 percent the previous week.
Fund selling totaled at least 30.0 million bushels with Griffin Trading a key seller of 21.0 million bushels of December, the traders said.
Corn closed 2-1/4 cents lower to 1/2 higher, with December down 3/4 at $2.96.

Corn attempted to rally in late dealings because the market was showing oversold signals. December's nine-day relative strength index (RSI) dropped to 15.815 points Tuesday, well below oversold levels of roughly 20 points. The 14-day RSI for December ended at 23.18 points.
December's four-day moving average (MA) ended at $3.00-1/2, 18-day at $3.15-7/8 and 40-day MA was at $3.28-3/4.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 88,000 contracts, down from 92,966 Monday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Refco Inc bought 1,000 December $3.50 calls at 1/2 cent and sold 1,000 December $2.90 calls at 11 to 12 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 37,000 contracts, down from 54,643 Monday.
